program.name: ndm_extractspikes
program.help:
Extract spike waveforms at previously-detected spike times (this creates .spk files).
Spike times are produced by ndm_detectspikes and stored in the shared .res files. ndm_extractspikes re-extracts a waveform for every one of those spikes and writes .spk; it does not detect, and errors if no .res exists yet. Because the spike times are method-independent, the extraction engine (method: standard, sdiff, or stderiv) may differ from the one used for detection, and ndm_extractspikes may be run several times with different methods to produce waveforms in different domains, each reusing the same .res.
The engine (method) and, for sdiff/stderiv, the spatial-derivative order (methodOrder) are set in the session's ndm_extractspikes program node; they are not declared here. Extraction needs no threshold or noise-window parameters — those belong to ndm_detectspikes.
PARAMETERS
# inputExtension
Extension of the data file read for extraction, without the leading dot (default fil, i.e. <session>.fil). Set it to an alternative, externally-processed source (e.g. car.fil or filtered.dat) to extract from that file instead. The source must be high-pass filtered like the usual .fil; ndm_extractspikes does not filter it.
# flatRunMax
Post-extraction filter: drop spikes with more than flatRunMax identical consecutive samples on any channel, checked in the raw source window (inputExtension) at the spike time and in the freshly extracted waveform. The raw check finds dropped-out channels, zero fill and stuck lines, which a spatial derivative hides by mixing the dead channel with its neighbours. ~20 separates channel dropouts from short zero runs at zero crossings. 0 or unset = off.
# dedupSamples
Post-extraction filter: drop a spike within dedupSamples samples of the previous kept one (the earlier is kept). Unset = 0 (identical positions only); -1 = off.
Because the .res is shared by every waveform variant of the group, dropped spikes leave the shared .res AND every other per-spike file of the group still at the original count -- .spk/.fet/.clu/.clc of any method and post-group stages -- with the same mask, so the set stays row-aligned. A file at the filtered count is left as is; a file at any other count is a different spike set and is reported, not touched. Symlinked aliases are filtered once. The original spike times are kept once as <res>.prefilter. Run by process_spikefilter.py.
METHOD TOKENS
The method may be qualified so the transform is stated in the artifact name rather than inferred: stderiv_S<order> runs the plain spatial derivative (orders 1-3) and leaves any per-group sdiffPairs unused, while stderiv_C<order> applies the session's sdiffPairs pattern -- order 4 for a single-partner pattern, order 5 for a reference-set pattern (one written with '+'). Outputs are stamped with the full token, e.g. <session>.spk.stderiv_C4.<group>.
Orders 4 and 5 are derived from the pattern itself and cannot be requested through methodOrder; a plain "stderiv" keeps the historical behaviour of applying whatever sdiffPairs the groups define.
